sonnet.name: learnable_entanglers_with_group_zzz
sonnet.desc:
The seed ansatz uses fixed (non-parametrized) CZ gates for entanglement, meaning the only trainable interaction structure comes from single-qubit RY/RZ rotations — the entangling pattern itself cannot be learned or tuned per upload/repeat block. This severely limits expressivity, especially since each of the 6 blocks (3 uploads x 2 repeats) gets independent parameters but the same static entangling topology.

This edit:
1. Replaces the fixed CZ gates on all 12 hardware-native edges with parametrized CRZ gates (same wires), giving the circuit trainable entangling strength per edge per block — directly increasing expressive power for the interactions that matter most for classification.
2. Introduces four three-qubit ZZZ (collective ZZZ rotation) gates that each connect qubit 0 (class_2's own readout qubit) with one qubit from READOUT_GROUP_0 and one qubit from READOUT_GROUP_1. This explicitly builds trainable higher-order (3-qubit) correlations across the three class-readout groups, which is well motivated since the fixed linear readout separates qubits into these exact groups — the ansatz should learn correlations between the groups, not just within them.
3. To offset the added CRZ/ZZZ parameters and control the total parameter budget/overfitting, the pre- and post-entangling RZ layers are changed from 9 independent per-qubit parameters each to 3 shared parameters each (one per readout group), since within-group qubits play symmetric roles in the fixed linear readout and don't need fully independent phase parameters.

Net effect: parameter count per block goes from 27 to 31 (186 total vs 162), a modest increase, but the added parameters directly target learnable entanglement and cross-group correlation — the two structural elements missing from the seed's fixed-CZ design — which should improve accuracy and reduce the train/test gap.

sonnet.name: parametrized_entangler_diagonal_fix
sonnet.desc:
The seed block wraps a fixed CZ entangling layer with independent pre- and post- RZ layers. Since RZ and CZ are both diagonal in the computational (Z) basis, they commute completely — the pre-RZ, CZ, and post-RZ all mutually commute, so the pre/post RZ split contributes no additional entangling structure beyond a single combined RZ layer (they only matter through interference with the *next* upload's RY/RX layers, but the two independent RZ sets are largely redundant with each other). This wastes ~9 parameters per block on redundant degrees of freedom while the actual inter-qubit entangling structure (CZ) has zero trainable parameters at all.

This edit (1) removes the redundant duplicate RZ layer (keeping a single RZ layer after entangling, which still has full expressive power once combined with the next feature-map RX layer), and (2) replaces the fixed, parameter-free CZ entangler with a parametrized CRY entangler on the same native edges. CRY is non-diagonal (it conditionally rotates population between |0> and |1> of the target based on the control), so — unlike CZ/CRZ — it directly creates entanglement that changes the marginal Z-expectation values, giving the optimizer real control over inter-qubit correlations relevant to the 3-class readout groups. Net parameter count per block goes from 27 (9 RY + 9 RZ_pre + 9 RZ_post, no entangling params) to 30 (9 RY + 12 CRY + 9 RZ_post), a modest increase that is now used for a genuinely more expressive entangling structure rather than a redundant phase layer.

sonnet.name: parametrized_entanglement_crz
sonnet.desc: Replace the fixed (non-parametrized) CZ entangling gates with parametrized CRZ gates on the same hardware-native pairs, and drop the post-entanglement RZ layer to keep the parameter budget reasonable. Fixed CZ gates provide static entanglement whose strength cannot be learned, limiting the ansatz's ability to adapt the amount of correlation it builds between qubits to the task. Making the entangling interaction trainable (CRZ) lets the optimizer learn how strongly to correlate each native pair, which should improve expressivity for the class boundaries defined by the fixed linear readout groups, while remaining native-hardware-compatible. Removing the redundant post-entanglement RZ layer (which was previously somewhat redundant with the pre-entanglement RZ + RY block for capturing single-qubit rotation freedom) keeps the total parameter count from growing too much (162 -> 180), maintaining comparable optimization difficulty and depth while adding genuine flexibility where it matters most: at the entangling layer.

sonnet.name: trainable_entangling_crz
sonnet.desc:
The seed block applies RZ_pre, then a fixed (non-parametrized) CZ, then RZ_post on every hardware edge. Since RZ and CZ are both diagonal in the computational basis, they commute, so RZ_pre and RZ_post on a given qubit always collapse into a single effective RZ (their sum) around a fixed-angle CZ — half of the RZ parameters are provably redundant and only slow optimization without adding expressivity. Meanwhile, the CZ entangling gates have no tunable parameter at all, limiting how much entanglement strength the circuit can learn.

This edit removes the redundant RZ_pre layer and instead promotes every hardware-native two-qubit connection to a trainable CRZ gate. This keeps essentially the same circuit depth/structure (RY layer -> entangling layer -> RZ layer) but converts previously wasted local phase parameters into genuinely useful, learnable entangling strengths, which should improve expressivity and thus train/val/test accuracy without a large increase in parameter count (30 vs 27 params per block).

sonnet.name: parametrized_entanglers_remove_redundant_rz
sonnet.desc:
The seed block has a "pre-entanglement RZ" layer applied before the fixed CZ gates and a "post-entanglement RZ" layer applied after them. Because RZ is diagonal in the computational basis and CZ is also diagonal, these two operators commute regardless of gate ordering. This means the pre-RZ layer contributes nothing that the post-RZ layer cannot already express (RZ(a) followed by CZ followed by RZ(b) is functionally identical to CZ followed by RZ(a+b)), so 9 parameters per block (54 total across 6 blocks) are essentially wasted, hurting parameter efficiency and possibly making optimization harder without adding expressivity.

I replace the redundant pre-RZ layer + fixed CZ gates with parametrized CRZ two-qubit gates on the same hardware-native edges. This turns the previously fixed (non-trainable) entangling structure into a trainable one, letting the model learn how strongly each pair should interact, which should improve accuracy while removing the wasted, functionally-redundant pre-RZ parameters. Net parameter count per block goes from 27 (9 RY + 9 pre-RZ + 9 post-RZ, non-parametrized CZ) to 30 (9 RY + 12 CRZ + 9 post-RZ), a modest increase that trades useless parameters for useful entangling degrees of freedom.

sonnet.name: hub_cross_entangler_zzz_link
sonnet.desc:
Replaces the fixed EfficientSU2-style block (independent RY + two RZ layers + 12 untrainable CZ gates) with a more expressive, better-structured, and shallower block that respects the fixed readout structure.

Key design choices, motivated by the readout groups (class_0 = mean Z over {2,3,7,8}, class_1 = mean Z over {1,4,5,6}, class_2 = Z on qubit 0):

1. Single-qubit layer: independent RY then independent RZ on every qubit (18 params) — gives each qubit a general rotation (combined with the RX from the feature map, this spans a full single-qubit rotation basis), same as before but without a redundant third RZ layer.

2. Entangling layer, using the fact that the 12 native edges naturally split into (a) 4 "hub" edges connecting qubit 0 (the sole class_2 readout) to every qubit in the class_0 group {2,3,7,8}, and (b) 8 "cross" edges connecting the class_0 group to the class_1 group. Instead of fixed, non-trainable CZ gates, we use trainable CRZ gates:
   - 4 independent CRZ parameters on the hub edges (0,2),(0,3),(0,7),(0,8), since qubit 0 alone determines class_2's score, these interactions are the most important to learn precisely.
   - 4 shared CRZ parameters over the 8 cross edges (grouped into pairs with similar topological role), giving parameter-efficient but still trainable entanglement between the two readout groups.

3. One three-qubit ZZZ interaction on (0, 3, 5) — one representative qubit from each of the three class-readout groups — with a single shared parameter, to let the circuit directly learn class-vs-class correlations that pairwise gates cannot easily express.

This keeps the parameter count per block at 27 (identical to the original 27, so total N_PARAMS=162 is unchanged and safely under any parameter budget) while cutting the gate count per block from 39 to 27 (18 single-qubit + 8 two-qubit + 1 three-qubit), which reduces circuit depth, improves trainability, and is expected to reduce the train/test generalization gap while giving the optimizer more useful entangling directions (trainable instead of fixed CZ) to fit the 3-class boundaries.

All two-qubit gates use only hardware-native pairs; the three-qubit gate uses unrestricted wires as permitted.

sonnet.name: add_cry_entangling_layer
sonnet.desc: The current block only uses diagonal two-qubit entanglers (CRZ) plus a handful of ZZZ terms; diagonal gates alone cannot rotate populations between computational basis states within a single block—their effect on Z-expectation values only shows up through interference with the RY layers of *subsequent* blocks. Adding a genuinely non-diagonal, amplitude-mixing controlled rotation (CRY) directly after the CRZ/ZZZ layer gives the ansatz real within-block entangling power to correlate populations across qubits, which should help decision-boundary shaping for 3-class separation. To keep the parameter budget efficient, the 12 hardware edges are split into the same 3 groups used for the RZ pre/post layers (4 edges per readout-group), sharing one CRY angle per group (3 new parameters per block instead of 12), so the added expressive power comes with only a modest (~10%) parameter increase.

sonnet.name: crz_backbone_zzz_correlator
sonnet.desc:
Building on the best-performing candidate so far (independent RY + full CRZ entangling layer over all 12 hardware edges + independent post RZ, 180 params, test_acc 0.61, val_acc 0.65), this version keeps that exact high-performing backbone unchanged (since it clearly outperformed the grouped-RZ / CZ variants) and adds a *cheap* explicit three-body correlation term to better couple the three readout regions.

Key structural insight from the fixed connectivity graph: qubit 0 (the sole class-2 readout qubit) is only hardware-connected to the four class-0 readout qubits {2,3,7,8}; the four class-1 readout qubits {1,4,5,6} are never directly connected to qubit 0, and never to each other — all group-crossing information must flow through class-0 qubits. This means the two-qubit CRZ layer already builds strong 0↔group0 and group0↔group1 couplings, but there is no native way to build simultaneous three-way (0, group0, group1) correlations with only two-qubit gates. Since three-qubit gates in this ansatz language have no connectivity restriction, we add four unrestricted `ZZZ` (collective exp(-iθ/2 ZZZ)) gates, each touching qubit 0, one distinct class-0 qubit, and one distinct class-1 qubit — covering all 8 non-anchor qubits exactly once. All four ZZZ gates share a single parameter, giving a nearly-free but structurally meaningful addition (only +1 parameter per block vs. the 180-param backbone, i.e. 186 total).

This keeps circuit depth modest (4 extra 3-qubit MultiRZ ops, largely parallelizable across disjoint wire sets) while giving the optimizer a direct handle on 3-way class interactions that were previously only reachable indirectly through chained 2-qubit gates and re-uploading.

sonnet.name: ry_post_rotation
sonnet.desc: The current ansatz block is: RY (pre-rotation) -> CRZ (entangling) -> RZ (post-rotation). Since CRZ and RZ are both diagonal in the computational (Z) basis, the RZ post-rotation layer commutes with the final PauliZ measurement and only has an effect through subsequent non-diagonal gates (RX feature map / RY of the next block) — for the very last block of the last upload it is essentially a no-op with respect to the read-out. This wastes expressive capacity. Replacing the post-rotation RZ layer with an RY layer keeps the parameter count and circuit depth identical, but makes the post-rotation non-diagonal in the Z basis, so it can directly reshape the entangled state right before measurement (standard "rotate-entangle-rotate" hardware-efficient pattern). This should let the ansatz make better use of the CRZ-induced correlations for the fixed Z-expectation readout, potentially improving both accuracy and the train/test generalization gap without any parameter overhead.

sonnet.name: add_sparse_zzz_triple_correlation
sonnet.desc: Add a single sparse three-qubit ZZZ (collective exp(-iθ/2 Z⊗Z⊗Z)) interaction per ansatz block, targeting one qubit from each readout-relevant group: qubit 0 (class_2 readout), qubit 2 (class_0 group), and qubit 4 (class_1 group). This directly injects a higher-order correlation term between the three class-discriminating qubit groups without violating the two-qubit hardware connectivity constraint (three-qubit gates are unrestricted). Since it uses a single new parameter name, it only adds 1 parameter per block (6 extra total across l=3, p=2), a modest cost (180->186 params) for potentially better discrimination and expressivity, consistent with the prior program that also added ZZZ gates and improved validation accuracy (0.65 vs 0.61) despite similar test accuracy. Here we add only one ZZZ (vs 4 in the second seed) to keep the parameter/depth overhead minimal while still testing whether triple correlations help.

sonnet.name: crz_symmetry_sharing
sonnet.desc:
Reduce CRZ parameter count by tying together structurally-analogous entangling
edges. The 12 hardware-native CRZ gates are grouped into 6 role-based pairs:
two "hub" pairs where qubit 0 fans out to its four neighbours ((0,2)&(0,7) and
(0,3)&(0,8)), and four "outer-ring" pairs connecting the remaining leaf qubits
((1,3)&(1,8), (2,4)&(2,6), (3,5)&(4,8), (5,7)&(6,7)). Each pair shares a single
parameter name, halving the CRZ parameter count per block from 12 to 6. This
tests whether structurally similar edges can profitably share a rotation
angle, cutting total parameters by 36 (186→150), which should reduce
overfitting/generalization gap and improve parameter efficiency while
retaining full connectivity coverage and circuit expressivity.

sonnet.name: none
sonnet.desc:
Revert to the better-performing "independent pre-rotation RZ" structure (which scored 0.60, higher than both the seed with post-RZ only and the current version with grouped RZ + 4 ZZZ gates), and add exactly one sparse three-qubit ZZZ correlator per block instead of four. The previous attempt with 4 ZZZ gates plus grouped/shared RZ pre/post rotations increased circuit depth dramatically (75 vs 41) without any accuracy benefit, likely because MultiRZ decomposes into several CNOTs each, quadrupling that overhead for little added expressivity, while the parameter-sharing reduced degrees of freedom too aggressively in the entangling-adjacent layer. Instead:
1. Restore independent (non-shared) RZ pre-rotations on every qubit (9 independent params) since this configuration measurably outperformed both the fully-shared grouped-RZ version and the version with post-RZ only.
2. Drop the post-entanglement RZ layer entirely (it added little identifiable benefit across seeds).
3. Add only a single ZZZ triple-qubit rotation per block linking one representative qubit from each class-readout group: wires [0, 2, 5] (qubit 0 = class_2 readout; qubit 2 is in class_0's readout group; qubit 5 is in class_1's readout group). This directly injects a genuine three-body correlation term relevant to the 3-way classification decision boundary while only adding ~+1 conceptual gate (and a modest, bounded decomposition depth, not 4x it).

This keeps total parameter count similar to the current version (186) but should substantially reduce depth relative to the current (4x ZZZ) version, and should preserve/improve the accuracy benefit seen from independent pre-RZ rotations.

sonnet.name: add_post_entangle_ry_layer
sonnet.desc:
The current best-performing ansatz (RY -> RZ_pre -> CRZ) leaves a fully diagonal
phase block (RZ_pre + CRZ) whose information can only be converted into
population/Z-expectation changes by a subsequent non-diagonal (RY) gate.  For
all blocks except the very last one in the circuit, this conversion happens
"for free" via the next block's leading RY layer.  However, for the final
block (upload=2, repeat=1) there is no subsequent RY before the Z-expectation
readout, so the accumulated CRZ/RZ_pre phase information from that last block
is largely wasted at measurement time.  Adding an explicit post-entanglement
RY layer (independent parameters, matching the earlier EfficientSU2-style
seed) lets every block -- especially the last one -- convert its entangled
phase structure into measurable population changes, which should improve
expressivity and final test/validation accuracy without touching connectivity
constraints.  This mirrors the "RY_post" idea from the very first seed but
keeps the RZ_pre phase-encoding layer that empirically raised accuracy over
that seed (0.60 vs 0.56), aiming to combine the benefits of both variants.

gpt56sol.name: readout_aligned_iqp
gpt56sol.desc: Replace the inefficient rotation ordering with a compact IQP-inspired block.
